text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- The widow of Kurdish leader Abdul Ghassemlou, who was asassinated in Vienna in 1989, said Austria encouraged Iran to further murders abroad. The ruling Social Democrats and Conservatives refuse to reopen the case.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima said a new export drive should not cost the state anything.
- The cooperation of grocery chains Loewa and Meinl has been called off as the two companies could not agree on important points.
- Labour unions and the Chamber of Labour are against promoting the introduction of Europe's single currency.
- Job institute AMS expects fewer apprenticeships to be available this year compared to last year.
- Longer shop opening hours are helping the big chains while small shops are suffering.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV plans to expand production at its petrochemicals group PCD.
- Metal producer VA Tech will raise its dividend to 30 schillings as growth and profits reached record levels.
- Building societies report ten percent more investments in the first quarter compared to the same period last year.

- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl plans to start an investigation into why the police set free the killers of three Kurdish leaders. Opposition parties demand a special investigation into the affair by parliament.
- Although taxpayers have been hard-hit by the government's austerity measures, Austria still cannot be sure of making the Maastricht criteria in time, a research institute says.
- There are rumours that bank Bawag's plans to take over the government's stake in postal savings bank PSK has the support of Chamber of Economy president Leopold Maderthaner.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische managed to improve its market position last year and will raise its dividend for the third year in a row.
- President Thomas Klestil's doctors say he has been completely cured of his pneumonia and would now be ready to go for another term in 1998.
